newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. seen drafting welfare recommendations by Oct.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. seen drafting welfare recommendations by Oct.

text.p: New York's task force on welfare, which is studying how the new federal bill will affect the state, is expected to report to Gov. George Pataki by early to mid-October, a state official said Wednesday.

John Signor, a spokesman for the state budget division, said the task force, which is chaired by the budget director, Patricia Woodworth, is analyzing the various options that states have under the federal welfare rules.
The group's recommendations are expected to cover a range of issues, from food stamps, to how legal immigrants will be handled, to childcare for welfare recipients.

Pataki, who had estimated that the extra costs that will result from the federal changes will be in the hundreds of millions of dollars, plans to call a special legislative session after the elections to enact his welfare reforms.

The new federal welfare bill shifts to a system of block grants, imposes work requirements and limits benefits for immigrants. States that submit their plans, which are due on July 1, before the deadline stand to reap extra funds and avoid costly penalties.

The governor last week predicted New York would meet the new work requirements, which oblige states to have 25 percent of the people who collect welfare working or enrolled in a work program during the first year.
As a result, the New York expects to maximize a $2.4 billion block grant.
Further, the state last Friday said it met the new federal rules for stiffening requirements for Food Stamps with one day to spare.
